messages.author: 04bb02334f7e0d5a
messages.subject: Refit model with test= "standard
parts:
Hi there,

I am working on a multigroup CFA using Lavaan. Please note that my data is ordinal and I have quite a few missing values.

I can't show you the entirety of my model because the scale I'm using is copyrighted, but here is a mock sample using the syntax that I used:

model <- 'Anxious=~ Q15_STD + Q20_STD + Q35_STD + Q31_STD + Q35_STD 
  Depressed =~ Q4_STD + Q42_STD + Q30_STD + Q70_STD
  Social=~ Q47_STD + Q50_STD + Q64_STD +Q54_STD'

In reality, I have a total of 112 items and 8 latent variables/subscales

When I run this code: 
allgroups <- cfa(model, missing = "FIML", fixed.x=FALSE,  meanstructure= TRUE)
summary(allgroups, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures= TRUE)

I get this warning: fit measures not available if test = "none"

if I run this code: 
allgroups <- cfa(model, missing = "FIML", fixed.x=FALSE,  meanstructure= TRUE)
summary(allgroups, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)
fitmeasures(allgroups, fit.mesaures="all")

I get this warning: please refit the model with test="standard"

I would really appreciate some help ASAP!

Thanks in advance,
Molly

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Refit model with test= "standard
parts:
You did not supply the data, which should be the raw data given that you use FIML. I can reproduce your error using the example in the help page of cfa().

Add "data =" and specify the data frame. E.g. suppose the raw data is in a data frame rawdata:

allgroups <- cfa(model, data = rawdata, missing = "FIML", fixed.x=FALSE,  meanstructure= TRUE)

Omitting "data =" is also OK as it is the second argument:

allgroups <- cfa(model, rawdata, missing = "FIML", fixed.x=FALSE,  meanstructure= TRUE)

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Refit model with test= "standard
parts:
Finding the estimates in a model with both ordinal variables and missing data handled by FIML sometimes can be quite difficult, and more so if the number of variables is large. It may take very long to find the solution, and sometimes it may just fail. The issue may be more a model+data one rather than a lavaan one.

In the summary() output, did you see something like this?

"lavaan 0.6-11 ended normally after X iterations"

If you do not even see this, then other error messages may not be that informative because many other functions on results usually assume that the optimization ended normally.

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)
